candidates.title: Alpha: Linear learning-rate warmup may stabilize SGD within one epoch
candidates.summary: Use cosine learning-rate decay from the reference rate across the one-epoch update steps; the smoothly decreasing step size may improve SGD's final accuracy within that epoch. Compare accuracy only on the synthetic task.
candidates.mechanism: A cosine schedule gradually reduces the step size over the epoch, which may limit late updates from overshooting useful parameter values.
candidates.closest_work: Learning-rate warmup schedules in stochastic gradient training; the closest setting and evidence for short-run synthetic logistic regression require literature review.

candidates.title: Zebra: Heavy-ball momentum converges faster under a fixed update budget
candidates.summary: With the same training data, epochs, and batch size, heavy-ball momentum may reach higher explore accuracy than the project's reference SGD within the fixed update budget because accumulated gradients can move farther along consistent directions.
candidates.mechanism: Heavy-ball momentum accumulates a velocity from successive gradients and may accelerate progress when gradient directions remain aligned.
candidates.closest_work: Classical heavy-ball momentum and momentum methods for stochastic optimization; applicability to this tiny synthetic logistic-regression setup must be checked.
